He received orders from Song Gongming, the Timely Rain, to come and look after Brother Li. If you took him away under guard and delivered him to the authorities, how could my brother return and face Song Gongming? That is why we resorted to this stratagem. Just now Brother Li meant to take advantage of the moment and kill you, but I would not let him strike. He killed only those militia men. If you return, you will certainly face prosecution, and there will be no one to rescue you. You would do better to come up the mountain with us today, place yourself under Song Gongming, and join our band. We can establish three more taverns devoted to gathering news, good or ill, and guiding traveling men of honor up the mountain. If the court dispatches government troops to suppress us, they can report how the forces are advancing so that we may prepare. The western hills cover a broad area, so let the brothers Tong Wei and Tong Meng take a dozen or so companions and open a tavern there; let Li Li take a dozen or so companions and open one south of the mountain; and let Shi Yong take some ten attendants and open one in the northern hills. Each place must also establish a waterside pavilion and signaling arrows to receive boats, and whenever urgent military intelligence arises, it must be reported with all speed. Three great passes shall be established before the mountain, with Du Qian placed in overall command of their defense. He is not to be reassigned for any other duty and must not leave his post without permission, day or night. Tao Zongwang shall supervise the labor crews, excavating inlets, improving waterways, opening channels, repairing the walls of the encircling fortress, and building the main road before the mountain. He comes from a farming household and has long experience in such work. Jiang Jing shall manage the treasuries and granaries, overseeing disbursements and receipts, the accumulation of stores by the thousands, and all written accounts and calculations. Xiao Rang shall prepare all official documents, passes, and written agreements for inside and outside the stronghold, above and below the mountain, and at the three guarded passes, as well as the roster numbers of chiefs great and small. Jin Dajian shall be charged with carving and making all military tallies, official seals, plaques, and related articles. Hou Jian shall oversee the making of robes, armor, banners of the five colors, and other such equipment. Li Yun shall supervise construction of all houses and halls at Liangshan Marsh. Ma Lin shall supervise the construction and repair of warships large and small. Song Wan and Bai Sheng shall establish a camp at Golden Sands Beach. Wang the Stunted Tiger and Zheng Tianshou shall establish a camp at Duck’s Beak Beach. p.src: Though but a courier, he holds no place in the ranks of soldiers. All his life a stranger in foreign lands, his two legs forever pay their debt to the road. When an inspector comes and goes, a black-flowered rattan staff bears his proclamation tablet; when a marshal’s headquarters marches to war, a yellow silk banner bears the character of command. Though home lies a thousand li away, he reaches it before the sun has shifted far; with urgent military intelligence, not even a quarter-hour is lost. At dawn he eats millet in Shandong; by evening he is eating goose pears in Wei Prefecture.

Beside a path below the hillside stood a burly man with a round head and large ears, a straight nose and square mouth, fine brows and wide-set eyes, a slender waist, and broad shoulders. Dai Zong hurriedly turned back and asked, “Good sir, we have never met before. How do you know my humble name?” The man answered excitedly, “So you truly are the Magic Traveler!” He dropped his spear and bowed to the ground. Several months ago, I met Master Gongsun Sheng at a roadside tavern, and we drank together. He told me in detail how Lords Chao and Song of Liangshan Marsh welcomed worthy men and treated them with such loyalty. He wrote me a letter and told me to go join the stronghold, but I have not dared enter rashly on my own. Master Gongsun also said, ‘At Lijia Crossing there has long been an inn kept by Zhu Gui, who guides those wishing to join up the mountain. The stronghold also has a chief charged with recruiting worthy men and swiftly carrying reports. He is Warden Dai, known as the Magic Traveler, who can cover eight hundred li in a day.’ When I saw your extraordinary pace just now, I called out to test my guess, never imagining that you truly were that honored brother. By heaven’s favor, I have met you when I least expected it.” Dai Zong said, “Master Gongsun Sheng returned to Jizhou on private business and has sent no word at all. Lords Chao and Song have now ordered me to come to Jizhou, inquire after him, and bring him back to the stronghold. All my life I have been headstrong: whenever I see injustice on the road, I must go to the victim’s aid. For that reason everyone calls me ‘Third Brother Who Stakes His Life.’ I came away from home with my uncle to trade in sheep and horses, but unexpectedly he died on the journey and our capital was lost. Unable to return home, I have drifted to this place and now make a living selling firewood in Jizhou. Since I have had the honor of making your acquaintance, I must tell you the truth.” Dai Zong said, “The two of us came here on business and were fortunate enough to meet you. How can a hero such as you ever rise in the world while stranded here selling firewood? You would do better to venture out into the world of rivers and lakes, and make the latter half of your life a happy one.” Shi Xiu said, “I know only a little spear and staff and have no other abilities. How could I ever attain success and happiness?” Dai Zong said, “In times like these, true worth goes unrecognized: first, the court lacks wisdom; second, treacherous ministers block the way. I am merely a man of scant ability, yet in a fit of indignation I went to join Song Gongming’s band at Liangshan Marsh. Now we weigh out gold and silver for equal shares and change into fresh suits of clothes. We await only the court’s amnesty, and sooner or later we shall all become officials.” Shi Xiu sighed and said, “Even if I wished to go, I have no way of gaining admission.” Dai Zong said, “If you are willing to go, I shall recommend you.” Shi Xiu said, “May I venture to ask the honored surnames of you two gentlemen?” Dai Zong said, “My surname is Dai and my given name is Zong. p.src: Now, Yang Xiong’s father-in-law, Old Pan, consulted with Shi Xiu about opening a slaughterhouse. Old Pan said, “Outside our back gate is a dead-end alley, and behind it stands an empty room. There is also convenient access to well water there, so it can serve as the slaughterhouse. We can have you lodge in that room as well, which will make it easy for you to keep watch over the place.” When Shi Xiu saw the place, he too was delighted by how truly convenient it was. Old Pan then found a former acquaintance to serve as an assistant, asking Shi Xiu only to manage the accounts. Shi Xiu agreed. He summoned the assistant, had the meat counter, water basins, and chopping blocks brightly painted in blue and green, sharpened a great many knives and implements, put the counter in order, cleaned up the slaughterhouse and pigsties, stocked them with more than ten fat hogs, chose an auspicious day, and opened the butcher shop. All the neighbors and relatives came to hang red decorations and offer congratulations, and they feasted and drank for a day or two. Everyone in Yang Xiong’s household was pleased that Shi Xiu had opened the shop. There is nothing more to relate of this for the moment. From then on, Old Pan and Shi Xiu attended to their trade. Time sped by unnoticed, and before long more than two months had passed. Late autumn was giving way to winter, and Shi Xiu had clothed himself in new garments from head to foot, both indoors and out. One day, Shi Xiu rose at the fifth watch and went to an outlying county to buy pigs. When he returned home three days later, he found the shop closed. When he went inside to look, he found that the butcher shop’s chopping blocks had all been put away, and the knives, implements, and other equipment had likewise been stored. Shi Xiu was a shrewd and observant man. At the sight of this he understood at once, and thought to himself, “As the saying goes, ‘No man stays in favor for a thousand days, nor any flower red for a hundred.’ My elder brother is away on official duties and pays no heed to household affairs. My sister-in-law must have seen me wearing all these new clothes and said something about it behind my back. And when I failed to return for two days, someone must have carried tales and stirred up gossip. It seems they have grown suspicious and stopped doing business. I shall not wait for them to speak their accusations aloud. I had better take my leave first and return to my native place. As the old saying has it, ‘Where is the man whose heart remains constant forever?’” Shi Xiu had already driven the pigs into the sty. He went to his room, changed his clothes and footwear, packed his bundle and baggage, carefully drew up a full and clear account book, and entered the house through the rear. Old Pan had prepared some simple wine and meatless dishes, and invited Shi Xiu to sit down and drink. Old Pan said, “You have wearied yourself traveling far and worked hard driving the pigs back.” Shi Xiu replied, “Father, it was only my duty. For now, please take this full and clear account book. If there is the least selfish deceit in it, may Heaven and Earth strike me dead.” Old Pan said, “Why should you speak so? Nothing at all has happened.” Shi Xiu said, “I have been away from my native place for five or seven years. Now I wish to go home for a visit, so I have come especially to return the accounts. I shall take leave of my elder brother tonight and depart early tomorrow morning.” When Old Pan heard this, he burst out laughing and said, “You are mistaken. Stay a while and listen to what this old man has to say.” The old man then poured forth a great many words, though they cannot all be recounted here. And thus it came to pass that a valiant man repaying a debt of gratitude raised his three-foot blade, while a monk who broke his vows was sent down to the Nine Springs. But what did Old Pan say in the end? Listen to the explanation in the next chapter.
